title.narrative: Provision of emergency livelihood support to the most vulnerable drought-affected households (pastoral communities) in rural villages of Bosaso District, Puntland State, Somalia

description.narrative: ltpgtThe project is aims at providing emergency lifesaving livelihood support to 1400 households /8400 persons (2315women, 2137 men, 1935 boys and 2013 girls) worst drought affected pastoralistoral communities in Af-Urur, Dalwayn, Galgala, Yalho, Kobdhexaad, Ciiradhame, Geesaqabad, Jeedaal, Kalabayr and Jiingadda rural villages of Bosaso, by providing them with emergency unconditional cash transfers of transfer value of $65 per household/ month for three months successively to support their immediate availability and access to food and avert further household depletion by selling their animals at throw away prices. The 1400 beneficiaries of UCT will additionally be provided with fodder of 50kg for 2 months to prevent their animals from death, improve their health/body conditions, and boost their livestock production.lt/pgtltpgtltspangtltbrgtlt/spangtlt/pgtltpgtltspangtThe project will be implemented in close convergence through coordination with WASH, Health and Nutrition partners at the project-targeted locations in Bosaso, where the targeted pastoral households will receive Water for their livestock from water points managed by the WASH partners and Health and Nutrition services from respective Health and Nutrition partners offering the services at the project-targeted locations in Bosaso. The project will prioritize female-headed households, pregnant and lactating women (PLWs) children aged between six months and five years who are particularly vulnerable to health and nutrition-related risks and face a significant risk of malnutrition-related health complications as well as families with persons with disabilities. Moreover, the project will ensure protection by ensuring the inclusive participation of socially marginalized communities, particularly minority clans, as well as people with disabilities who face risks of exclusion and isolation from humanitarian services and are significantly affected by the current devastating drought conditions.lt/spangtlt/pgtltpgtltspangtltbrgtlt/spangtlt/pgtltpgtThe project comes at a time when there are significant funding shortfalls, while humanitarian needs are very dire and overwhelming, with an estimated 887,000 people living in severely affected areas in 16 districts affected by the current devastating drought (FAO/SWALIM). Moreover, a total of 28,410 persons in rural villages of Bosaso are stressed/ IPC 3, while 20,290 are in crisis/ IPC 4, and 4,060 persons are in emergency (FSNAU post-Gu Assessment report of 23rd September 2025), hence the need for timely life-saving livelihood support to avert a possible disaster. The project will be implemented for a period of six months. lt/pgt
